givemotion: judge-1 (as A): Hits every beat with clean palette use: the stacked wall build (0.31–0.94s), the alternating word slides and one-character-per-frame typing in Beat 2 (4.69–7.19s), crisp band wipes with dividers drawing across (12.5–12.9s), and a well-timed bar-sweep reveal that turns into the underline (22.0–24.06s). The knockout title (1.56–2.3s) sits on a solid Ink field with the wall barely showing, so it reads as dim, muddy text rather than a reveal. The handover at 4.06s shows a blank label card with wall slivers at the edges instead of a real push, and the OCTOPUSES-to-spine handover at 15.94s is a nearly empty frame with a stray band before the wall rebuilds out of half-drawn shelf lines (16.2s). Category names sit at the band's old position while the band expands (10.0s ANIMALS at the bottom), which weakens the hierarchy.

judge-2 (as A): The most faithful and coherent piece. Clean push-in match cut at 4.06s, Beat 2 type and tracking widen (7.0–7.6s), a tidy lift-and-dock into the bands (7.8–8.4s), a category name that stays inside its expanding band (10.94s), a decimal pulse at 12.6s, the spine landing back in place at 16.2s, and a neat bar-sweep outro and underline (22–24s). Weaknesses: the knockout title (1.56–2.3s) is dim slate-on-ink, so the wall barely reads through it and it doesn't fill the width; level transitions get busy with horizontal coral sweeps (9.69s, 10.0s); the floor-plan dot is in row 2, not row 5.

judge-3 (as B): Every beat and the coral thread are present: the decimal point pulses (12.6s), the final bar sweeps across and settles as an underline (22.0–24.0s), and the floor-plan path pops its ÷10 marks (17.6–18.4s). The re-split, done with slate panels sliding in from the right, reads as busy and unclear (10.0s key, 12.7–12.9s, 14.69s). The rolling counter shows broken half-glyphs ('1 IN 10A' at 9.69s, 14.69s, 12.9s), and MOLLUSKS gets cut off at the top of its band (12.6s). The push-in has not started by 3.8s, and the frame at 15.94s is nearly empty, so the handovers feel less tight.

judge-4 (as C): A readable knockout (2.0s), clean sliding headline words in Beat 2 and a solid outro sweep and underline (22.0-23.8s); the staggered band wipes add energy. The Beat 1 handover is compressed (no push-in at 3.8s, full coral with a blank card by 4.06s), and the band transitions get messy, with labels clipped at 12.6s and 12.9s and garbled counter frames (9.69s '1 IN 10A', 12.9s, 14.69s). The OCTOPUSES-to-spine handover passes through a near-empty frame (15.94s), and at 16.2s the spine floats across a shelf line instead of landing in its row.

judge-5 (as B): The band expansion in Beat 3 is the best of the three: the chosen band truly pushes the others out (12.3s) and new bands wipe in from the right (12.7s). The outro is clean (23.8s). But the knockout title barely reads, as dim slate letters on Ink (2.0s). At 3.8s there is still no push-in, only the slid-out spine. The return to the wall is broken: 15.94s is a nearly empty frame, and at 16.2s the Coral spine floats across a shelf line while the rows rebuild from the bottom. On the floor plan the dot sits mid-row below the shelf, not at the labelled end (17.2s), and the counter shows garbled mid-roll glyphs (9.69s, 14.69s).

judge-6 (as C): C hits every beat and has a literal handover: the OCTOPUSES band narrows into a spine and the wall rebuilds around it (15.94–16.56s). The outro matches the other two (22–24s). The knockout type is dim slate on Ink, centred, and far short of the full width the brief asks for (1.56–2.3s), so the opening reads as muddy. Beat 3 transitions show broken wipes from the right with partial Coral fragments on the bands (9.69s, 10.0s, 11.56s, 14.69s). The counter roll catches as garbled glyphs ('1 IN 10Ø' at 9.69s, a stacked '1,0/10' at 12.9s, '1 IN 10Ø ..' at 14.69s), and CEPHALOPODS appears almost immediately after the decimal pulse. The floor-plan dot sits between shelf rows rather than on the fifth row (17.2–20.3s), and the spine floats off its shelf line at 16.2s.
remotion: judge-1 (as B): Closest to the brief: the knockout title is cut into a band with the spine wall visible above and below (2.0–2.3s), and the camera push at 3.8s, where the spine's label grows into the 594.56 card, is a real shared-element match cut. The wall rebuilds fully around the Coral spine in place (16.2s), and the outro bar shows its 90° rotation (23.44s) before settling as a clean underline. Weaknesses: a ghost 'BOOKS.' shows through under 'ONE.' during the wipe at 2.5s; the Beat 2 headline leading is so tight the lines almost touch (4.69–7.5s); at 12.8s the band reset has MOLLUSKS colliding with a divider line; and at 15.94s a floating Coral square looks unresolved. Beat 3 levels are legible and the counters hold well (10.0s, 13.44s).

judge-2 (as C): The best knockout (2.0–2.3s): the ink panel sits only behind the text rows, so the wall stays visible, and the camera push into the spine at 3.8s is the strongest handover of the three; the bar rotation reads well at 23.44s. Weaknesses: Beat 2 headline leading is so tight the lines nearly collide (4.7–7.7s), and leftover slivers remain after the wipe at 7.9s. In Beat 3 the category name jumps to band '0' after every re-split (9.06s, 10.31s, 12.2–12.7s), which misreads the digit logic, MOLLUSKS jumps across band boundaries at 12.8s, and the counter lags at 14.69s.

judge-3 (as A): The most complete and legible piece. The 'A MILLION / BOOKS.' cut-out sits over the live spine wall and reads clearly (2.0–2.3s), and the downward wipe to 'YOU NEED / ONE.' is clean (2.4–2.6s). The push-in at 3.8s shows a real match cut from the spine to the label card, and the band re-splits draw their divider lines cleanly (12.2–12.7s). Weaknesses: the Beat 2 headline is too small next to the card (4.7–7.2s), and the MOLLUSKS label is left hanging over band 2 while the stack resets (12.8s). Beat 4's floor plan feels small and flat.

judge-4 (as A): The most complete and cleanest build: the knockout type over the visible wall (2.0s, coral spine inside the K), a readable downward wipe to YOU NEED / ONE. (2.4-2.6s) and a real push-in match cut where the spine label becomes the card (3.8s). The Beat 3 bands fill the stack and re-split crisply (12.0-12.9s), and the outro bar sweep and underline are clean (22.0-23.8s). Type is undersized against the brief (Beat 2 headline, category names, outro about 105px not 190px), the knockout letters are low contrast, and a stray floating coral square appears during the wall rebuild (15.94s).

judge-5 (as C): It has the strongest opening. The knockout panel sits inside the wall, so the letters read well with spines showing through (2.0s). At 3.8s there is a real camera push into the spine with the label card growing, which is the best match cut here. The wall rebuilds cleanly around the spine (16.2s). But Beat 3's re-split logic is confusing: each new category jumps to band '0' (9.06s, 12.2s), the bands flood coral and then revert, and at 12.8s MOLLUSKS slides down over the digits. The Beat 2 headline leading is so tight the lines almost touch (5.3–7.7s), stray slivers of the headline remain at 7.9s, and at 14.69s OCTOPUSES appears while the counter still reads 1 IN 10,000.

judge-6 (as B): B has the strongest Beat 1. The type is a true knockout in Ink panels over the wall, the Coral spine shows through the 'I' (2.0–2.3s), the wipe to YOU NEED / ONE. is clean (2.4–2.6s), and the camera pushes into the spine and its label (3.8s), which is the best match cut of the three. Beat 3 transitions move well: the band grows to fill the stack and Coral sub-bands split it again (12.1–12.9s). The handover back to the wall and the floor-plan path with the ÷10 pops also hold up (15.94–19.7s). Weaknesses: the category name stays parked in band 0 after each re-split (9.06s, 10.31s, 14.06s), which suggests the wrong digit, and at 12.8s MOLLUSKS overlaps the band-2 label. The counter lags behind the band ('1 IN 10,000' while OCTOPUSES is already selected at 14.69s). The Beat 2 headline leading is cramped, and stray strokes are left over from the wipe at 7.9s.
hyperframes: judge-1 (as C): Structurally complete, with a good push-in handover (3.8s, spine body framing the label card) and a well-balanced Beat 2 layout (7.0–7.8s). The knockout title (1.56–2.3s) breaks up into sliced, doubled letterforms with an offset lower copy of 'BOOKS.', and is hard to read. Band changes rely on cross-fades that blend Coral and Slate into off-palette mauve and brown tones (9.69s, 10.0s bands 4–5, 11.56s, 12.0s band 9, 12.8–12.9s, 14.69s), which reads as muddy and goes against the brief's ban on generic fades. CEPHALOPODS is clipped in half at 14.06s and SCIENCE is gone by 10.0s, so not every label holds long enough. The outro reveal and underline are clean (22.0–23.8s).

judge-2 (as B): Strong camera push into the spine and card (3.8s), clean Beat 2 type and tracking (7.0–7.6s), a good wall rebuild at 15.9–16.5s and a solid outro. But the opening knockout (1.56–2.3s) is broken: sliced letters, shelf lines through the glyphs and a misaligned ghost copy of 'BOOKS.', all at the hook. Beat 3 uses translucent coral tints that go muddy on slate (9.69s, 12.0s, 14.69s), CEPHALOPODS is cut off at 14.06s, the number stays Ink during the squeeze (7.9s), and a ÷10 overlaps the 590–599 label at 19.69s.

judge-3 (as C): It has the strongest Beat 1→2 match cut, with the coral spine pushing into the frame around the card (3.8s), and a nicely hard-left Beat 2 layout (7.0s). The cut-out headline, though, breaks into pieces: shelf lines cut through the letters and a ghost copy of 'BOOKS.' sits underneath, so it can't be read (1.56–2.3s), and it switches to 'YOU NEED' without a visible wipe. Bands blend into muddy mauve and brown tints that look off-palette (10.0s, 12.0s, 14.69s), CEPHALOPODS is cut off (14.06s), and Beat 3 runs late, still on level 1 at 10.0s. Two ÷10 marks overlap at 17.9s.

judge-4 (as B): Strong handovers: a good push-in into the spine with the label as the card (3.8s) and a neat spine-to-dot morph onto the floor plan (17.0s). The knockout is broken, with letters cut up by shelf lines and a ghosted lower half on BOOKS. (1.56-2.3s), and YOU NEED arrives as a hard switch at 2.4s, not a wipe. Bands blend into muddy tints while changing colour (10.0s, 12.0s band 9), CEPHALOPODS is clipped and unreadable during a band expansion (14.06s), and timing runs late (still re-splitting SCIENCE at 10.0s).

judge-5 (as A): The most complete and faithful version. It has a clear spine-to-label match cut (3.8s, the Coral spine grows into the field with the card already inside), docked number and counter beats that read cleanly (10.0s, 12.0s), the dot sitting on the 590–599 row end in a tidy floor plan (17.2s), and a solid bar-sweep and underline ending (22.0–23.8s). Weaknesses: the knockout type at 1.56–2.3s is muddy and hard to read, with shelf lines slicing the letters. Beat 2 crams small type into the top half and leaves the bottom empty (5.3–7.4s). The band re-split never pushes the other bands out; it just floods them, and a half-cut CEPHALOPODS shows at 14.06s. The sweep's reveal edge trails well behind the bar (22.5s).

judge-6 (as A): A tells the story in a clear chain. The Coral rectangle grows over the dimmed wall into the label card (3.8s). Beat 3 is the cleanest of the three: a single Coral band, a readable category name and a Mustard counter (10.0s, 12.0–12.4s). The outro bar sweep and its turn into an underline are tidy (22.0–24.0s). Weaknesses: the knockout 'A MILLION BOOKS.' (1.56–2.3s) looks sliced, with shelf lines running through the letters and a ghost copy offset below them, so it reads as glitchy rather than a clean cutout. The text swap at 2.3–2.4s is nearly a hard cut. The re-splits in Beat 3 bring back a semi-transparent reddish band that looks like a fade (9.69s, 11.56s, 14.69s), and the mid-wipe CEPHALOPODS at 14.06s is clipped.
